subject: DPA negotiation: DR/backup carve-out proposal — NexaCloud
messages:
From: Benjamin Lewis <benjamin.lewis@nexacloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@nexacloud.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed DPA language for DR/backup — NexaCloud

Hannah —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Per our procurement team’s request, attached is the NexaCloud proposed DPA with an explicit carve-out in Section 6.3 addressing backup/DR retention and disaster recovery restores (we included the operational procedure in a separate PDF). The carve-out is intended to preserve our ability to keep immutable backups for up to 90 days in a cold archive for operational recovery and to comply with our internal audit policies.

Key highlights we flagged in the attachment: 
- Retention window for cold DR backups: up to 90 days from creation; backups encrypted at rest.
- Deletion/erasure: live customer data will be deleted on termination per the listed retention schedule; backups will be overwritten/rotated and only accessible to a narrow ops group during restoration events.
- Cross-border transfers: we reference standard SCCs and an EU-US data transfer addendum.

We’d like to get your redlines ahead of DocuSign so we can avoid iterative cycles. Can your legal and security teams review and flag any operational requirements that would prevent us from keeping the 90-day cold archive carve-out?

Attachments: NexaCloud_DPA_Proposed.docx (docx), Nexa_DR_Procedure.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Benjamin
Benjamin Lewis
Head of Legal Operations, NexaCloud

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Benjamin Lewis <benjamin.lewis@nexacloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA language for DR/backup — NexaCloud

Ben —

Thanks for sending this over. We reviewed the doc and attached our redlines (see Redwood_DPA_Redlines_20261130.docx). High level response: we understand the operational need for a short-term cold archive for DR, but we need clearer guardrails to ensure customer deletion requests and legal holds are respected.

Requested clarifications in the redlines: 
- Narrow the ‘90-day cold archive’ language to explicitly exclude use for analytics or product development and limit access to SRE/IR during an incident.
- Add stricter logging and audit controls for any restoration activity (who, why, what data).
- For EU data, require confirmation that SCCs+addendum permit the backup retention approach — we added a suggested clause to tie transfer legal basis to the specific backup purpose.
- Add a rollback/overwrite schedule and a one-time certification step after termination that verifies backups containing customer data were purged or rendered unrecoverable consistent with the technical measures described.

We’d also like to run a short technical call (30m) with your ops folks to walk through the DR procedure PDF. Can you propose times Thursday/Friday PST?

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_20261130.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships (Contracts) — Redwood Inference

From: Benjamin Lewis <benjamin.lewis@nexacloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA language for DR/backup — NexaCloud

Hannah —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and detailed redlines. Our ops lead (copied here earlier in a separate message) confirmed they can join a technical call — Friday at 10:00am PST works for us. We reviewed your redlines and can accept most, but we have two sticking points: 

1) The certification after termination: we can provide a time-bound attestation that backups were rotated and no recoverable copies remain, but we cannot always provide a forensic-level, per-customer cryptographic destruction certificate for cold snapshots that are stored in immutable stores managed by our provider.

2) The 90-day window: we can reduce exposure by agreeing to a default 60-day rotation unless otherwise required by regional regulation; however, for high-criticality recoveries (disaster impacting multiple regions), we need the ability to extend retention to 90 days for a limited period with documented approval from NexaCloud’s CISO.

We are comfortable adding additional audit logging and a restoration access workflow to the DPA as you requested. We’ll highlight proposed alternative language in the next draft.

Ben

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Proposed DPA language for DR/backup — NexaCloud

Karthik/Grace —

FYI — Nexa offered compromises on the retention window (60d default, 90d for escalated multi-region events with CISO approval) and pushed back on a per-customer cryptographic destruction certificate for cold immutable snapshots. They’re fine with stronger logging and a restoration approval workflow.

Quick asks from our side before the call: 
- Karthik: draft a short paragraph that ties the rotation/overwrite process to our termination obligations and that asks for the attestation scope they can provide (operations-level attestation vs. cryptographic proof).
- Grace: confirm whether the proposed restoration approval (CISO sign-off for 90d extension) is acceptable from a risk perspective or whether we should require a board-level escalation for any step beyond 60 days.

We’ll join Ben on Friday at 10am PST to walk the DR procedure and aim to get a near-final DPA ready for e-signature.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Benjamin Lewis <benjamin.lewis@nexacloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@nexacloud.com
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 18:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA language for DR/backup — NexaCloud

Hannah —

Thanks to you and your team for the productive call. Per our discussion, we updated the DPA to: 
- Default retention for cold DR backups: 60 days.
- 90-day extension allowed only after documented approval by NexaCloud CISO and a joint incident declaration between both parties.
- Added an operations attestation clause on rotation/overwrite within 30 days of termination (attestation will describe processes and provide confirmation that routine rotations occurred; it will not be a cryptographic proof).
- Added a restoration access audit trail requirement and role-based access controls for any restore events.

We’ve uploaded the redlined DPA to DocuSign for signature: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000&v=2

If Redwood can accept the attestation instead of cryptographic destruction certificates, we can proceed to execute. Let me know and I’ll send the DocuSign invite to your signatory.

Best,
Benjamin
